rules.description: Governance implementations must not import compiler or binding implementation modules.
Repository quality tooling must orchestrate contracts and processes rather than import a semantic compiler implementation.
A generated artifact must not appear among its own authoritative sources or generator inputs.
Contained-task records and templates must remain in designated governance locations.
New top-level implementation directories require an explicit architecture declaration.
The canonical Rust kernel must not depend on host-language bindings or repository tooling implementations.
The canonical interop bridge may transport versioned contracts and call the public kernel, but must not depend on historical bindings or repository tooling implementations.

The curated Rust package must compile the canonical core/src implementation through one same-source crate root, keep internal stages private, and must not restore binding-owned parsing, analysis, planning, emission, or standard-library semantics.
The C package must remain a thin native adapter over the canonical interop bridge and must not restore its retired semantic compiler copy or third-party regex/JSON engines.
The C++ package must remain a type-safe RAII facade over the governed C/native package and must not restore its retired compiler stages or downloaded semantic dependencies.

The TypeScript package must remain a thin browser-safe adapter over the governed raw WebAssembly ABI and must not restore its retired parser, compiler stages, validator, emitter, CLI fallback, or runtime regex simulation.
The Python package must remain a thin adapter over the governed native ABI and must not restore its retired parser, compiler stages, validator, emitter, CLI fallback, or runtime regex simulation.
CI and release workflows must use canonical profiles as certification authority, derive product evidence only from their structured artifacts, and retain both forms without redefining pass or fail.
Every current or future binding must remain a thin adapter: implementation-like semantic paths and declarations are forbidden outside explicitly classified facade declarations.
Frozen implementation-era fixtures remain explicitly non-normative history and cannot become product, generation, profile, or certification authority.
Retained implementation-era corpora are data-only history and cannot become product, normative, generation, profile, or certification authority.
Canonical LSP code actions, formatting, island extraction, and their closed evidence must not import the transitional Python binding.
The extension package generator, packaged-runtime certification, and authored server adapters must not import the transitional Python binding as a semantic or runtime dependency.
Canonical LSP diagnostics, hover, lifecycle, and their evidence must not import the transitional Python binding.
Completion, navigation, symbols, references, semantic tokens, and their closed evidence must not import the transitional Python binding.
Specification schemas may reference only specification-owned schema contracts, never generated implementation output.
The regex-compatible frontend owns only versioned compatibility syntax and cannot define canonical semantic or target authority.
The Semantic STRling contract owns versioned source syntax and mapping but cannot implement parsing or redefine canonical semantics, targets, or runtimes.
New parser, compiler, analyzer, planner, or emitter implementations under tooling require explicit architecture review.
Java and Kotlin expose only request-recording facades over one pinned shared JVM/native bridge; historical semantic copies and alternate native or regex routes are forbidden.
C# and F# expose request-recording facades over one C# NativeLibrary bridge; historical semantic copies and alternate native or regex routes are forbidden.
Go, Dart, and Swift expose semantic-free absolute-path transports over strling.c-abi v1; historical semantic copies and alternate execution routes are forbidden.
Ruby, PHP, Perl, Lua, and R expose semantic-free absolute-path transports over strling.c-abi v1; historical semantic copies and alternate execution routes are forbidden.

Every toolchain-registered binding and supporting transport is classified by the canonical route manifest, remains thin, uses an approved canonical transport, and is covered by an enforced route rule.
Canonical frontend mappings and core source boundaries must converge through Semantic IR before analysis and planning, then select a target profile before producing a TargetArtifact.
JavaScript test/compiler dependencies removed with the implementation-derived oracle architecture must remain absent from both the root manifest and its lock graph.
Retired donor generators, Omega reports, migration comparators, and the closed P19 Perl waiver must remain absent.
Every canonical profile and the product-certification producer graph must retain the architecture, contract, semantic-authority, generation, and documentation hardgates exactly once.
